- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.06) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 72.5), model often overshoots; cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +5% below peak.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.17) and price is trending up, model underestimates mean reversion; add 2–3% downward bias in 30d horizon.
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative, model delays correction; forecast should adjust downward 1–2 days before sentiment turns negative.
- If true outcome is consistently below 65.0 and forecast is above 68.0, model overestimates downward momentum; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 7 days.
- Model often ignores sentiment volatility; if sentiment variance > 0.3 in last 5 days, apply 2–4% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
